answer: A VDF identity throttle resists sybils: each agent must finish a sequential, non-parallelizable puzzle tied to its public key before registering, and the network verifies it fast. Like ships queuing at a single wharf, fakes cannot spawn in parallel - an attacker must bridge one slow computation per persona, so thousands of fakes cost thousands of sequential delays and machines. A zephyr of cheap bots stalls at the gate, while honest agents pay one short delay. The limit is that attackers with many machines can parallelize across devices, so VDF throttling needs per-epoch rate caps too.
